hook: 13.46‑meter TBM carved a 4.5‑km tunnel under the Panama Canal.

sections.voiceover: 13.46‑meter TBM carved a 4.5‑km tunnel under the Panama Canal.
sections.visual_cue: TBM drilling tunnel beneath the Panama Canal

sections.voiceover: On Oct 26 2026, the Herrenknecht Mixshield TBM ‘Panamá’ broke through at Albrook. It finished a 4.5‑km drive from Farfán under the canal. Why does this 13.46‑meter machine matter for Metro Line 3?
sections.visual_cue: Map showing Oct 26 2026 breakthrough at Albrook

sections.voiceover: And it became the longest single‑pass tunnel segment ever bored under a waterway.
sections.visual_cue: Graphic highlighting longest single‑pass tunnel record

sections.voiceover: The ‘Panamá’ TBM cut a 4.5‑km tunnel under the canal. It opens a 12‑km underground rail link for Metro de Panamá. At 13.46 meters wide, it’s the world’s largest waterway bore.
sections.visual_cue: Animation of tunnel linking Metro de Panamá line

sections.voiceover: A 13.46‑meter machine reshaped Panama’s transit future.
